summary: This document retires the use of GOST R 34.10-2001 (ECC-GOST) and GOST R 34.11-94 in DNSSEC. It updates RFC 5933, which is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9906 retires GOST R 34.10-2001 and GOST R 34.11-94 for DNSSEC. It says not to create records using these algorithms and explains how validators must treat records that use them.

questions: why was gost removed from dnssec
which gost algorithms are deprecated in dnssec
what should a dnssec validator do with gost records
what did rfc 9906 change in the gost registries
subtitle: Retires two older GOST algorithms from DNSSEC signing and validation.

tldr.problem: GOST R 34.10-2001 and GOST R 34.11-94 were deprecated in 2012 and are no longer recommended for DNSSEC.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC prohibits their use for DNSSEC records, requires validators to treat related records as unsupported or insecure, and updates both IANA registries.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9906 updates RFC 5933, which it identifies as Historic, and retires ECC-GOST use in DNSSEC.

today: RFC 9906 is a Proposed Standard from November 2025 and updates RFC 5933, which this document identifies as Historic.

sections.title: Why ECC-GOST Is Retired
sections.content:
RFC 5933 defined GOST R 34.10-2001, also called ECC-GOST, and GOST R 34.11-94 for DNSSEC. The RFC says these algorithms were deprecated by Russian standards authorities in August 2012 and superseded by the 2012 GOST algorithms.

RFC 9906 updates RFC 5933 and states that the older algorithms are no longer recommended for DNSSEC. It does not change the requirement levels for the newer GOST algorithms described in RFC 9558.
sections.plainLanguage: The two older GOST algorithms were superseded in 2012. This RFC retires their use in DNSSEC while leaving the newer GOST algorithm requirements unchanged.

sections.title: Signing and Validation Rules
sections.content:
GOST R 34.11-94 MUST NOT be used to create Delegation Signer (DS) records. Validating resolvers MUST treat DS records using it as insecure. If no other accepted DS algorithms are available, records below the delegation point are treated as insecure.

GOST R 34.10-2001 MUST NOT be used to create DNSKEY or RRSIG records. Validators MUST treat signatures made with it as unsupported; if no other accepted signatures are available, the associated resource records are insecure.
sections.plainLanguage: Do not create DS, DNSKEY, or RRSIG records using the retired GOST algorithms. Validators treat them as insecure or unsupported as specified, rather than treating them as valid signatures.

sections.title: Operational and Registry Changes
sections.content:
The RFC says zone operators using ECC-GOST should switch to algorithms that remain supported. It says DNS registries should prohibit clients from uploading and publishing ECC-GOST-based DS records.

IANA marks algorithm number 12, GOST R 34.10-2001, and digest value 3, GOST R 34.11-94, as deprecated. The registry entries state that they MUST NOT be used or implemented for DNSSEC signing, validation, or delegation as listed.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators using these algorithms should move to supported algorithms. The IANA algorithm and digest registries now mark the older GOST entries deprecated.
